title: Chelsea vs. Man Utd Player Ratings: Blues Punish Miserable Red Devils
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray11:01 AM EDTThe Blues earned a valuable win. / Adam Davy/PA Images/Getty ImagesLisandro Martínez’s foolish red card condemned Manchester United to a disastrous 2–0 defeat to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, heaping even more pressure on the under-fire Michael Carrick.

Both clubs entered Saturday’s affair desperately scrambling for respite, but the stakes were considerably higher for the Red Devils and Carrick after an eight-match winless streak. The return of Bruno Fernandes from the naughty step offered encouragement for the away side, and it was the 32-year-old who squandered the best chance of the early stages when firing over from close range.

A vastly improved performance from consecutive three-goal defeats yielded more United opportunities as the half progressed, with Amad Diallo twice testing Chelsea’s goalkeeper before Matheus Cunha saw his near-post finish ruled out for offside following VAR intervention. At the other end, Estêvão was denied by the linesman’s flag when tapping into an empty net.

Inexplicably, neither team was able to open the scoring during an action-packed first half, and United’s profligacy came back to bite them just five minutes after the restart. Some amateurish defending allowed Morgan Rogers to glide into the penalty area, after which he executed an exquisite dinked finish to put Chelsea in front.

Things quickly went from bad to worse for the visitors, too. Martínez, just four minutes after his first booking, was shown a second yellow card for recklessly—and completely needlessly—barging into Wesley Fofana at a corner, with Cole Palmer converting the subsequent penalty.

Estêvão saw another strike ruled out for offside as Chelsea sought to further gloss the scoreline, but they were ultimately forced to settle for just the two-goal victory as they piled yet more misery on United.

United never help themselves. / Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesUnited’s ability to implode in remarkable and dramatic fashion is unrivaled in the Premier League.

After humiliating defeats to Como and Bournemouth, they were in dire need of a positive reaction, and for the first 45 minutes in west London, Carrick received exactly that. United were comfortably the stronger side from the off, dominating the goal-mouth action and keeping Chelsea relatively quiet up until the halftime whistle.
But this beleaguered United team need no invitation to capitulate, and they delivered their latest collapse shortly after the restart.

United’s defense parted like the Red Sea as Rogers casually strolled through to fire the hosts ahead. An absent midfield offered little protection, but there can be no excuses for a rearguard which gifted the Englishman the freedom of Stamford Bridge to score a crucial opener.
Carrick’s tactical acumen has been deservedly questioned—even by his own captain—but he can’t be blamed for the moment of utter chaos which ruled out any chance of a United comeback.

Martínez, who publicly took aim at the club’s recruitment only a few weeks ago, neatly wrapped up three points for Chelsea courtesy of his baffling red card. Without even looking at the ball as the home side swung a corner into the box, the Argentine, leading with his arm, collided into Fofana, deservedly earning a second booking following VAR intervention and giving up a spot kick.
It was yet another example of just how rotten United are at their core—both in the boardroom and dressing room—and a rash decision which could easily hammer the final nail in Carrick’s coffin.
Estêvão earned an increasingly rare start. / Chris Lee/Chelsea FC/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Mike Penders—7.4: Made some strong saves and one excellent stop to keep United out. Went much better than last weekend’s Premier League outing.
RB: Josh Acheampong—8.3: Handled Matheus Cunha effectively and dovetailed nicely with Estêvão ahead of him.
CB: Wesley Fofana—8.1: Made not one but two blunders which should have gifted United—and more specifically Amad—an opening goal during the first 45 minutes. Very fortunate they went unpunished.
CB: Levi Colwill—7.5: Helped Chelsea earn a rare clean sheet with a commanding performance.
LB: Marco Palestra—7.0: Struggled for much of the match. Out of position too frequently, while also offering very little in the attacking third.
